english: You step in behind the counter.
There are compartments filled with ruined tin boxes. In the back, there's a complicated set of tubes and pipes combining into some type of tea-making machine.
A brewer. Not often you get to see those these days.
For such a fine (and expensive!) piece of machinery to break. A shame.
The machine catches your attention. Search it.
Machines. Very complicated.
You understand it, however. All of this is easy to you.
So, this is where they sell tea. Right here.
Is it worth it to investigate here?
Yes. Now investigate.
Yes. Do it.
I'll have a sweet with cream, please, Snell says nasally.
He leans over the counter. "Oh, make that half-cream, actually. My tummy's sensitive today."
He's making fun of humans and their love of milk.
Not the best joke, but he'll like you more if you play along.
Oh, the goblin's kidding!
Time to make a different, better joke. That'll be smooth.
I don't work here, Snell.
Good one.
(Answer in a snobby tone.) "We only serve Hill-sourced oatmilk, sir."
But you're a goblin. Don't you want some green tea?
Yeah- I, he mutters.
He considers explaining his joke to you.
He's surprised by that answer. Did he think you were a barista?
He sighs. "Just check the damn counter."
Thanks. See if you find something behind the counter.
The goblin looks at you, then looks at the counter.
Then looks at you again.
That's called a double-take. Good job.
Look at his face. Pure shock.
Good one, Cleric.
He waves his claw. "Check the counter."
For a short instant he actually thought you were funny. Damn.
The goblin laughs.
Fake laughter.
That's funny! Because I'm green.
His smile drops. "Check the damn counter."
Sensitive.
(Look at the surface.)
(Look over the machine.)
(Look into the charred boxes.)
E-(Stop looking around the shop counter.)
There's a slab of wood covering the stone base of the countertop.
More like charcoal at this point.
It was once finely sanded Brachen. Now ruined.
But the stone still stands. Strong. Steadfast.
Pipes and levers melted. Glass shattered.
This was once a fine work of engineering.
(Check the pipes.)
M-That's it.
A metal of some kind.
Copper pipes. Expensive. Once shiny, now charred and bent.
Hand-crafted. You can see the markings of a rounded hammer across it. A lot of care went into this machine.
This is where you put the tea leaves.
As you lean in, you don't see much beyond some burnt muck through the cracks.
But you do smell something.
It smells awful.
Your stomach turns.
An intense scent.
Why does it smell like that?
(Lean in. Closer.)
Do I have to?
(Move away from the chamber.)
It contains something foul.
You do not know what.
Move... away.
You must go closer. Know the scent.
Come on. Don't.
Good idea. Perhaps you can identify the contained flora... or perhaps fauna?
(Inhale the horrible smell.)
You smell the disgusting burnt muck through the gaps of your helm.
It smells like disgusting burnt muck.
Bad. This is not good.
You know this is bad.
<shake>Oouuhh...</shake> Bad.
What smells foul- makes your nose stronger.
That's NOT true.
Holy hells, stop shoving your face into... whatever this shit is!
(Move back.)
Your knees shake. But you stand.
Take care of yourself better.
As you turn around, you find the goblin glaring at you with a worried expression.
I'm going to pretend I didn't see that.
You really do not.
Clues can be found in the foulest of places.
You do so.
There's a metal valve at the end. It's shut.
It's only shut when it's brewing. That means it was working during the explosion.
(Open the valve.)
(Leave it alone.)
You try to turn the valve, but it bends at an odd angle.
Wait. That is not how a valve is supposed to feel.
It's... stuck?
You are the hammer. This valve is the nail.
(Force it.)
(Be careful.)
I'm not messing with this thing. (Leave it.)
What are you doing? your companion asks as you lift the hammer above your head.
(Bring it <shake>down</shake>.)
With an intense precision and egregious power - you SMASH your hammer onto the valve.
If a machine does not work, you make it work.
Oh no.
You put pressure on the valve as you turn the little lever.
Only with finesse can you tame a machine like this.
Because you're such an expert at that.
You carefully put pressure on the valve as you turn the little lever.
The machine returns your indifference.
Suddenly, you hear a snap.
A tiny piece of copper comes flying towards you, hitting your helmet with a dink.
You totally let it do that.
Oh. There's more...!
Shit. Step back!
The valve bursts open, releasing an oozing pile of tea, ash, and gods-only-know-what-else onto the floor.
Gods be damned, Snell mutters, and holds his nose.
The scent is particularly awful.
Avoid.
Avoid.
Try to survive.
You leave it for now.
You leave the machine where you found it.
Tin boxes full of tea leaves.
Or... they're supposed to be. The heat from the explosion has melted both the tin and its contents.
It's just ash now.
Damn. Was hoping at least one of these would be intact.
Selling tea is a legit side hustle. The margins are bonkers.
FOULNESS.
But nothing you cannot stand.
You smell the fetid, melted ooze.
This is disgusting...!
The goblin is dry heaving next to you.
(Try your best not to puke.)
NO.
Your mind goes blank.
Your mouth waters.
Everything goes black.
Cleric...!
Did I faint?
Yes.
That's not good.
You will wake.
Your time is not yet.
Not until the coin is flipped.
What?
Oh...
You open your eyes.
Snell is standing over you.
You good?
I don't believe you. But cool.
Let's keep going, okay?
Alas.
You persevere.
Yeah, great job, man.
Now stop smelling WEIRD SHIT...!
You are NOT enjoying it.
The floor behind the counter is now covered in a layer of ashy mulch.
Hm. This is what victory smells like. You have won.
You will tell the tale of The Chamber and the Valve to your offspring.
This will be your legacy. This is who you are.
It better not be.
Strong veto on that one.
Ugh. What did I gain from this?
A loud ding comes out of the machine as the last dribble of ooze exits the canister.
It's still operational? What the hell...?
Operational? More like leaking innards.
A death knell.
After the bell, a box opens up at the top of the machine.
Inside you see dry tea leaves.
It's the steam leaves. They're supposed to add extra flavor.
And that scent... they are Ukkul leaves. From Kargamesh.
Yummy.
In your tummy. Tea is good.
Wait... this thing was ready to go.
Doesn't that mean it was being used during the explosion?
The machine was ready? Perhaps it was being used during the explosion.
(Grab the leaves.)
Mm. Alright, well. That means those tea leaves are evidence.
The goblin is correct for once.
Always good to have proof.
Evidence, huh...
Snell stares at you.
Yeah. Pick up the leaves, Cleric.
You need to get better at listening.
What? He does NOT speak to you that way.
Oh. Right. Of course.
You don't tell me what to do.
Yeah. Of course.
I think I just did.
He sighs and takes a step back. "Fine. Whatever you do, don't take the leaves, Cleric."
Reverse psychology? What, does he think you're fi-
Thank you. (Grab the leaves.)
Damn it.
You carefully place the dry leaves in your pouch.
The goblin gives you a nod.
Now can we please not hang around this... goop.
